name: Man Maker
description: The man maker is a multi-movement dumbbell complex in which the athlete performs a push-up, a renegade row on each arm, a squat clean, and an overhead press — all in a single continuous sequence without putting the dumbbells down. It demands upper body pushing and pulling strength, anti-rotation core stability during the row, and total body power during the clean, making it one of the most comprehensive single-exercise conditioning movements available. It is used in advanced circuit training and high-intensity conditioning programs.

execution.starting_position: Stand with dumbbells on the floor, shoulder-width apart. Begin by hinging down to grip the dumbbells in a push-up starting position.
execution.setup_instructions: Use matching fixed dumbbells of moderate weight. Ensure adequate floor space.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a push-up position gripping both dumbbells on the floor.
Step 2: Perform one push-up — lower the chest to the floor and press back up.
Step 3: Perform a renegade row with the right arm — pull the right dumbbell to the hip while balancing on the left.
Step 4: Perform a renegade row with the left arm.
Step 5: Jump or step the feet forward to a squat position, clean the dumbbells to shoulder height, then press them overhead. That is one full rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on each push phase (push-up, row pull, press). Inhale between movements.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips during the renegade row — the hips must remain square to the floor
Using momentum rather than strength during the row phase
Rushing the transitions between movements — control each phase
safety_considerations: Very high demand on the shoulder girdle and core — a prerequisite of proficiency in all component movements.
Wrist neutral grip (dumbbells parallel to the body) reduces wrist stress in the push-up phase.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up range. Full row elbow retraction. Full overhead lockout on the press.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3–8 reps per set. Full recovery between sets — this is a maximal-effort complex.
coaching_cues: Lock out the press fully overhead
